result.approach:
Treat this as three concrete pieces, matching the scope list:

1) Confirm the current loop is actually unbounded. I don't have the retry code in front of me, so I can't point to the specific file/loop — that has to be checked before writing the fix, not assumed. What I'd look for: is this a custom while/recursive retry loop, or a job-queue-based retry (e.g. a queue library with its own retry semantics) that's been misconfigured (like max_retries set to -1/infinite, or a retry-on-failure re-enqueue with no counter)? The fix shape is different in each case, so this has to be pinned down first, not guessed.

2) Add a bounded max retry count. Whatever the mechanism turns out to be, the concrete change is: track an attempt count per delivery attempt (either a column/field on the delivery record if this is DB-backed, or the job queue's native attempt counter if it's queue-based), and stop re-enqueueing once attempts >= max. Sane default: 5 attempts with the existing backoff schedule if one exists, or a simple exponential backoff (e.g. 1m/5m/30m/2h/6h) if there isn't one already — I haven't verified whether backoff already exists, so this may just be 'reuse what's there' rather than new work.

3) Decide what happens on exhaustion. My default recommendation: mark the delivery as failed/terminal in whatever store tracks delivery status, log it with enough context to debug (webhook id, target URL, last error, attempt count), and increment a metric/counter that's already being watched or alerted on. I'd hold off on building a full dead-letter queue (storage, replay mechanism, UI) unless one already exists somewhere in the system — that's a bigger piece of infra than 'stop retrying forever' calls for, and nothing in the ticket says failed deliveries need to be replayable later. If dead-lettering infra already exists elsewhere in the codebase, reuse it instead of the log+metric approach; that's an open question, not a guess I want to bake into the plan.
result.confidence: High that the right shape is: bounded counter + stop condition + terminal state + logging is the correct fix for 'retries indefinitely.' Low confidence on the exact implementation site and mechanism (custom loop vs job-queue retry config) since no code or system description was given — that has to be confirmed against the actual code, not assumed from the ticket text.
alternativesConsidered: Full dead-letter queue with persistent storage and a replay path — rejected for now as more infra than this ticket asks for; nothing here indicates failed webhooks need to be resurrectable later, and there's no evidence such infra already exists to extend.

Alerting/paging on exhaustion — rejected as the default; log + metric is enough to make the failure visible without assuming there's an on-call/paging setup this should hook into. Would revisit if that infra is confirmed to exist.
Just capping the backoff interval without capping attempt count — rejected, it doesn't fix the actual bug (indefinite retries), just slows them down.
openQuestions: Is the retry loop custom code or a job-queue library's built-in retry mechanism? Changes where the fix actually lives.
Does backoff already exist, or does that need to be added alongside the max-retry count?
Is there existing dead-letter/alerting infra elsewhere in the system that this should plug into instead of a plain log+metric?
Is 5 attempts an acceptable default, or is there an existing convention elsewhere in the codebase for retry limits that this should match?
